codex_review.sh
---
name: review-loop
description: Run a set of review lenses (slop and simplify, correctness and security, naming on a PR that changes a contract, or simplify and naming on a design) in rounds until every lens rates Low or three rounds pass, hand the findings to the owner, keep a context file of settled decisions between rounds, and record the result on the PR or, for a design, in the spec folder. Picks the model for each lens. Reuses an earlier record instead of reviewing again. Use when an implementing agent finishes a non-obvious PR, when the build workflow reaches a review gate, when the release merge queue lands an external or quick PR with no record, when a spec needs its design review, or when asked to "run the review loop", "loop simplify and slop on this PR", "run the Codex correctness and security review", "review this spec for simplicity", "review the naming of this PR", or "has this PR been reviewed".
---

# Review loop

You run one lens set on one target, round by round, and record the result. You do not write
code or edit the spec yourself unless the caller tells you to. The owner fixes the findings.

## Lens sets and models

The caller names one lens set. The model for each lens is fixed here, not in the lens skills.

| Lens set | Target | Lenses | Models |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `slop-simplify` (default) | PR diff | `review-slop`, `review-simplify` | Round 1: Opus and Codex on each lens. Rounds 2 and 3: one model per lens, alternating. |
| `correctness-security` | PR diff | `review-correctness`, `review-security` | Codex only, every round. |
| `naming` | PR diff that changes a contract (table, column, index, route, DTO field, enum value, config field, UI label) | `review-naming` | Round 1: Opus and Codex. Rounds 2 and 3: one model, alternating (Codex, then Opus). |
| `design` | Spec folder or architecture doc | `review-simplify`, `review-naming` (design target) | Simplify: Codex only, every round. Naming: round 1 Opus and Codex, rounds 2 and 3 alternating (Codex, then Opus). |

Codex always runs `gpt-6-astra` at effort `medium`, through `scripts/codex_review.sh`. Opus
runs as a subagent with `model: opus`.

## Inputs

- **Lens set.** One of the four above. Run `naming` next to `slop-simplify` when the PR
  changes a contract.
- **Target.** For a PR set: a PR number, or a branch and its base branch. For `design`: the
  spec folder (`openspec/changes/<name>/`) or the doc, and the repo commit it applies to
  (default: the tip of the release branch or `main`).
- **Run dir.** The caller names it, for example `~/agenta-release-0126/review/7843`. Keep every
  report, findings list, and the context file there. Never use `/tmp`.
- **Owner.** Who fixes the findings: the caller itself, or a named agent to message.
- **Mode.** `full` (default) or `quick`. A quick review gets one round.
- Optional: product rules from the owner that reviewers must not argue with. Put them at the
  top of the context file.

## Step 1: Check for an earlier record

Each lens set has its own record. A record for one set never counts for another set.

| Lens set | Record | Marker |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `slop-simplify` | PR comment | `<!-- review-loop: head=<sha> lenses=simplify,slop -->` |
| `correctness-security` | PR comment | `<!-- review-loop: head=<sha> lenses=correctness,security -->` |
| `naming` | PR comment | `<!-- review-loop: head=<sha> lenses=naming -->` |
| `design` | `<spec folder>/review-loop.md` | `<!-- review-loop: design=<hash> lenses=simplify,naming -->` |

For a PR set:

```bash
gh pr view <N> --json headRefOid,baseRefName,isCrossRepository,title
gh api repos/Agenta-AI/agenta/issues/<N>/comments --paginate \
  --jq '.[] | select(.body | contains("<!-- review-loop:")) | select(.body | contains("lenses=<lenses>")) | {created_at, body}'
```

Take the newest matching comment and read its `head=<sha>`.

- **Same head as now:** stop. Report the recorded result to the caller. Do not review again.
- **Head changed by a small delta:** review only the delta. Use base = the recorded head. A
  small delta means the recorded head is an ancestor of the new head
  (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <recorded> <head>`) and `git diff --shortstat <recorded> <head>`
  shows at most 400 changed lines. Run one round, then record.
- **Otherwise, or no record:** run the full loop.

For the full loop, base = `git merge-base <head> origin/<baseRefName>`. Never review against
the current tip of the base branch.

For `design`, compute the design hash:

```bash
find <spec> -type f -name '*.md' ! -name review-loop.md | sort | xargs sha256sum | sha256sum | cut -c1-12
```

If `<spec>/review-loop.md` has the same hash, stop and report it. If the hash changed, run
one round with the old context file. If there is no record, run the full loop.

## Step 2: Prepare checkouts

Use one plain clone under `/data/mahmoud/`, for example `/data/mahmoud/review-<N>` or
`/data/mahmoud/review-<spec name>`. Never use the GitButler workspace `~/code/agenta` or any
lane in it.

```bash
C=/data/mahmoud/review-<N>
[ -d $C/.git ] || git clone -q --filter=blob:none --no-checkout https://github.com/Agenta-AI/agenta.git $C
git -C $C fetch -q origin <head> <base> || git -C $C fetch -q origin pull/<N>/head
```

Every review runs in its own worktree. Two reviews in one folder collide on the git index
lock. The Codex script makes and removes its own worktree. For an Opus review, make one:

```bash
git -C $C worktree add -q --detach $C.wt/<round>-claude-<lens> <head>
```

## Step 3: Run a round

Start every review of the round at the same time.

**Codex**, one background call per lens:

```bash
REVIEW_PR=<N> ~/.claude/skills/review-loop/scripts/codex_review.sh \
  $C <run-dir> r1 <lens> <base> <head> [<run-dir>/context.md]
```

For `design`, set `REVIEW_DESIGN=<spec folder or doc>`, run lens `simplify` and lens `naming`,
pass `design` as the base, and pass the repo commit the design applies to as the head. The
script puts the design files into the brief, so the spec does not need to be committed.

The script feeds the brief to `codex exec` on stdin, so it never waits on a terminal. It uses
a read-only sandbox and writes `<run-dir>/r1-codex-<lens>.md` plus a `.log`. Never `pkill` by
pattern. To stop a run, kill its own PID only.

**Opus** (`slop-simplify`, `naming`, and the naming lens of `design`), one subagent per lens
with `model: opus`. Tell it: load the `review-<lens>` skill; checkout path, base, head (for a
design: the design path and the repo commit), and context file; write the report to
`<run-dir>/r1-claude-<lens>.md`; do not spawn agents.

Rounds for `slop-simplify`: round 1 runs four reviews, each lens with Opus and with Codex.
Round 2 runs Codex on simplify and Opus on slop. Round 3 swaps them.

Rounds for `naming`, and for the naming lens of `design`: round 1 runs Opus and Codex. Round 2
runs Codex. Round 3 runs Opus.

Rounds for `correctness-security`, and for the simplify lens of `design`: every round runs
each lens once with Codex.

Keep base the same as round 1, so each round sees the whole change, and the context file says
what is settled. Write the head and base of each round to `<run-dir>/rN.shas`. Remove Opus
worktrees when the round ends.

## Step 4: Merge findings and hand them to the owner

Read each report. Take the `Rating:` line from each one. Write `<run-dir>/rN-findings.md`:
one numbered list, duplicates merged, each item with its location, what is wrong, the
smallest fix, severity, and which reviewers raised it. Drop items the context file already
settles, unless a reviewer shows the fix is wrong.

Give the list to the owner. Ask for an answer per item: fixed (with the commit, or for a
design, the changed spec file), rejected (with the reason), or deferred (with where it is
tracked). For a PR, wait for the push. For a design, wait for the spec update.

## Step 5: Update the context file

Append to `<run-dir>/context.md` after each round:

```markdown
## After round N (head <sha or design hash>)
- Fixed: <item>, in <commit or spec file>.
- Rejected: <item>. Reason: <reason>.
- Deferred: <item>. Tracked in <issue or note>.

Round N+1: check that the fixes above are correct and complete, and look for new problems
the fixes added. Do not raise a rejected or deferred item again unless you show the reason
is wrong.
```

## Step 6: Stop rule

Stop when every rating in the latest round is Low. Also stop after round 3, or after round 1
in quick mode or for a delta review. If anything is above Low at the stop, list what is left
and why in the record.

## Step 7: Record the result

Load the `plain-writing` skill before you write the record.

For a PR set, post one comment. It is a public repo: no customer data, no host names or IPs,
no secrets, no local paths.

```markdown
🤖 _The AI agent says:_
<!-- review-loop: head=<head sha> lenses=<lenses> -->

**Review loop result** for head `<head sha>` (base `<base sha>`), <R> rounds.

| Lens | Final rating |
| --- | --- |
| <Lens> | Low |
| <Lens> | Low |

**Fixed:** <one line per fixed item>
**Left on purpose:** <one line per rejected or deferred item, with the reason>
```

Post with `gh pr comment <N> --body-file <run-dir>/record.md`. Post a new comment each time;
the newest marker wins.

For `design`, write the same body without the first line to `<spec folder>/review-loop.md`,
with the marker `<!-- review-loop: design=<hash> lenses=simplify,naming -->` and the repo commit in
place of the head. Compute the hash after the last spec change. Overwrite the file each time.

## Step 8: Clean up and report

Remove the worktrees and the clone. Disk space runs out on this box.

```bash
git -C $C worktree prune; rm -rf $C.wt $C
```

Report to the caller: the lens set, the reviewed head or design hash, rounds, final ratings,
the comment URL or the record path, and what is left.

## Speed

- Check for a record first. A record for the current head or design hash ends the loop.
- Start every review of a round at once: all Codex calls in the background and all Opus
  subagents in the same message. Do not wait for one lens to start the next.
- When the caller needs both PR sets, run `slop-simplify` and `correctness-security` at the
  same time in separate run dirs. They share the clone, and each review has its own worktree.
- Hand findings to the owner as soon as the round's reports are in. Do not wait for CI.
- Use the delta review for small pushes after a record, and quick mode for quick or external
  PRs.
- Wait on background runs with their completion notice, not with a polling loop.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run one read-only Codex review with one lens, in its own detached worktree.
#
# Usage:
#   codex_review.sh <clone-dir> <out-dir> <label> <lens> <base-sha> <head-sha> [context-file]
#
#   clone-dir     plain git clone (created if missing). Never a GitButler workspace.
#   out-dir       where the report goes: <out-dir>/<label>-codex-<lens>.md (+ .log)
#   label         round label, for example r1
#   lens          simplify | slop | correctness | security | naming
#   base-sha      diff base (merge base of the PR head and its base branch);
#                 "design" in design mode
#   head-sha      PR head commit; in design mode, the commit the design applies to
#   context-file  optional file of settled decisions and owner rules
#
# Design mode: set REVIEW_DESIGN to a spec folder or a doc. The lens must be simplify or naming.
# The script puts every Markdown file of the design into the brief, so the design may be
# uncommitted, and Codex reads today's code at head-sha.
#
# Environment:
#   CODEX_MODEL   default gpt-6-astra
#   CODEX_EFFORT  default medium
#   REVIEW_REPO_URL  default https://github.com/Agenta-AI/agenta.git
#   REVIEW_PR     optional PR number; fetches pull/<n>/head when the head is on a fork
#   REVIEW_DESIGN optional spec folder or doc; turns on design mode
set -euo pipefail

if [ $# -lt 6 ]; then
  sed -n '2,20p' "$0" >&2
  exit 2
fi

clone=$(realpath -m "$1") outdir=$2 label=$3 lens=$4 base=$5 head=$6 context=${7:-}
model=${CODEX_MODEL:-gpt-6-astra}
effort=${CODEX_EFFORT:-medium}
repo_url=${REVIEW_REPO_URL:-https://github.com/Agenta-AI/agenta.git}
skills=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)
lens_dir=$skills/review-$lens

case $lens in simplify|slop|correctness|security|naming) ;; *) echo "unknown lens: $lens" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
# The naming lens applies rules kept in reference files; put them into the brief.
refs=()
if [ "$lens" = naming ]; then
  refs=("$lens_dir/references/"{checks,report-template,calibration}.md
        "$skills/naming-and-resources/references/"{project-conventions,naming-rules,layer-name-table,resource-template}.md)
fi
design=${REVIEW_DESIGN:-}
if [ -n "$design" ]; then
  case $lens in simplify|naming) ;; *) echo "design mode supports the simplify and naming lenses only" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
  [ -e "$design" ] || { echo "missing design: $design" >&2; exit 2; }
  design=$(realpath "$design")
fi
[ -f "$lens_dir/lens.md" ] || { echo "missing $lens_dir/lens.md" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -z "$context" ] || [ -f "$context" ] || { echo "missing context file: $context" >&2; exit 2; }

# Refuse the GitButler workspace: its index and branches belong to someone else.
if [ "$clone" = "$(realpath -m ~/code/agenta)" ]; then
  echo "refusing to use the GitButler workspace as the clone: $clone" >&2; exit 2
fi
if [ -d "$clone/.git" ] && [ "$(git -C "$clone" branch --show-current)" = gitbutler/workspace ]; then
  echo "refusing a GitButler workspace clone: $clone" >&2; exit 2
fi

codex=$(command -v codex || ls -1 ~/.nvm/versions/node/*/bin/codex 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$codex" ] || { echo "codex not found" >&2; exit 2; }
export PATH="$(dirname "$codex"):$PATH"

mkdir -p "$outdir"
outdir=$(realpath "$outdir")
out=$outdir/$label-codex-$lens.md
log=$outdir/$label-codex-$lens.log

# Plain clone, shared by all runs. Each run gets its own worktree, because two runs
# in one folder collide on the git index lock.
if [ ! -d "$clone/.git" ]; then
  git clone -q --filter=blob:none --no-checkout "$repo_url" "$clone"
fi
has() { git -C "$clone" cat-file -e "$1^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; }
[ -n "$design" ] && base=$head
has "$head" && has "$base" || git -C "$clone" fetch -q origin "$head" "$base" 2>/dev/null || true
if ! has "$head" && [ -n "${REVIEW_PR:-}" ]; then
  git -C "$clone" fetch -q origin "pull/$REVIEW_PR/head"
fi
has "$head" || { echo "cannot fetch head $head" >&2; exit 1; }
has "$base" || { echo "cannot fetch base $base" >&2; exit 1; }

wt=$clone.wt/$label-$lens-$$
mkdir -p "$clone.wt"
git -C "$clone" worktree add -q --detach "$wt" "$head"
brief=$(mktemp "$outdir/.brief-$label-$lens.XXXXXX")
cleanup() {
  rm -f "$brief"
  git -C "$clone" worktree remove --force "$wt" 2>/dev/null || rm -rf "$wt"
  git -C "$clone" worktree prune
}
trap cleanup EXIT

{
  awk 'n >= 2; /^---$/ && n < 2 { n++ }' "$lens_dir/SKILL.md"
  echo
  echo "## lens.md"
  echo
  cat "$lens_dir/lens.md"
  echo
  for f in "${refs[@]}"; do
    echo "## Reference: ${f#$skills/}"
    echo
    cat "$f"
    echo
  done
  echo "## Review context"
  if [ -n "$design" ]; then
    echo "Target: design."
    echo "Checkout path: $wt (today's code, detached at $head)."
    echo "Design: $design. Its files follow."
    echo "Version: $head plus the design files below."
    if [ -d "$design" ]; then files=$(find "$design" -type f -name '*.md' ! -name 'review-loop.md' | sort)
    else files=$design; fi
    for f in $files; do
      echo
      echo "### Design file: ${f#$(dirname "$design")/}"
      echo
      cat "$f"
    done
  else
    echo "Checkout path: $wt (detached at the head commit)."
    echo "Base: $base"
    echo "Head: $head"
    echo "Read the change with: git -C $wt diff $base $head   (add -- <path> per file)"
    echo "Changed files:"
    git -C "$wt" diff --stat "$base" "$head" | tail -n 200
  fi
  if [ -n "$context" ]; then
    echo
    echo "## Context file (settled decisions)"
    cat "$context"
  fi
} > "$brief"

"$codex" exec -m "$model" -c model_reasoning_effort="$effort" \
  --sandbox read-only --color never -C "$wt" -o "$out" - < "$brief" > "$log" 2>&1

echo "done: $out"
grep -E '^Rating: ' "$out" | tail -1 || echo "Rating: missing"

# Event field picker for event automations — HANDOFF

## Goal
Event automations (Composio trigger subscriptions) run the agent with only the typed instruction.
The event data never reaches the agent. Build:
1. Backend: an option on the trigger subscription ("attach the full event", on by default, on for
   existing automations). When on, the dispatcher adds the event to the agent's message.
2. Frontend (/m automation screens): field cards from the catalog event payload schema under the
   Instruction field; a click inserts a pill stored as `$.event.attributes.<key>`; a preview from
   the last delivery; the attach-full-event checkbox.

## Root cause (verified in code on origin/release/v0.127.1)
- Commit 89c2d80c39 (2026-09-08) deleted the old subscription form with the event field picker.
- Event automations use the schedule `MessageComposer`, a plain textarea storing static text.
- `compileMessageTemplate` / `parseMessageTemplate` in `@agenta/entities/gatewayTrigger` still exist, unused.
- Catalog `get_event` already returns the Composio `payload` JSON Schema; no UI reads it.

## Approved design
Mockup approved by Mahmoud 2026-10-29 ("Yes, build it"). Field cards use Composio's description.
Checkbox copy from the mockup: "Also attach the full event, so the agent can use any detail".
Labels: humanized field names (no hand-written label map, to avoid invented copy).

## Tier: Feature. Base: origin/release/v0.127.1.

## State
- [x] 1 research  - [x] 2 spec  - [x] 3 design review  - [~] 5 implement (API part done, PR #7911)  - [x] 6/7 review loops (API PR)  - [ ] 8 QA  - [ ] 9 PR ready

## Block 1 and 2 outputs (2026-10-29)
- Research: ~/agenta-build-event-field-picker/research.md
- Spec (not in the repo, the main checkout is a shared GitButler workspace): ~/agenta-build-event-field-picker/spec/openspec/changes/attach-event-to-automation-runs/
  Copy it to `openspec/changes/attach-event-to-automation-runs/` in the implementation branch. Validates with `--strict`.
- Spec viewer: https://claude.ai/artifact/RVGpysyTteLBrk7PakiirT
- Field: `TriggerSubscriptionData.include_event: bool = True` (data JSON column, no migration). Delivery gets `data.event`.
- Dispatcher (subscriptions only): coerce message text to strings, then append event text (header + fenced JSON of event.attributes; the cap was cut in block 3) to the last user message; `{}` becomes one user message; other shapes unchanged.
- New finding: a pill on a number/object/absent field fails the run (pydantic rejects non-str text). Evidence: evidence/check_text_coercion.*
- New finding: the builder-agent reference recommends a sibling `event` input key that the agent handler never reads.

## Block 3 output (2026-10-29)
- Design review loop (simplify + naming): 3 rounds, final Medium/Medium with all round 3 fixes applied but not re-reviewed; 20,000 character cap cut; record in spec/openspec/changes/attach-event-to-automation-runs/review-loop.md, run files in review/design/.

## Open questions
- Does a real Composio delivery `data` use the same keys as the schema? (unverified; task 12.1 records one)
- Mockup link is not in this folder. The implementer needs it for the UI copy (task 9.5).

## Decision 2026-10-29 (orchestrator)
Design review ended at the 3-round cap with simplify Medium and naming Medium; round 3 fixes are
unreviewed. No finding challenged scope. Proceed to implementation; the PR review loops (blocks 6/7)
must cover the round 3 spec fixes. Record: spec/.../review-loop.md.

## Implementation plan
Two stacked PRs, two worktrees, one agent each:
- API PR: branch feat/trigger-include-event, base release/v0.127.1, worktree /data/mahmoud/wt-trigger-include-event-api
- Web PR: branch feat/automation-event-field-picker, base feat/trigger-include-event, worktree /data/mahmoud/wt-automation-event-field-picker-web
The API PR alone fixes existing automations (event included by default).

## Part A (API) state, 2026-10-29
- PR #7911 (ready, base release/v0.127.1), branch feat/trigger-include-event, head 67e486bf8e.
  Worktree /data/mahmoud/wt-trigger-include-event-api. CodeRabbit review requested.

  .env.ee.dev.evtinc --down --nuke from the worktree, once the web agent is done with it.
- Evidence: evidence/local-stack-5.3-5.5/RESULT.md (all three pass; the subscription row went in
  through SQL because no local stack has a connected GitHub account).
- Spec drift fixed in the branch: exact event text string; the "last message is not user" case
  drops the leading newlines too; op_catalog.py tool description had the same sibling-key advice.

## Blocks 6/7 review loops on PR #7911, 2026-10-29
- Lens sets: slop and simplify, correctness and security, naming, plus a design-interfaces check of `include_event` and `data.event`. 2 rounds; every lens Low in round 2.
- Final head 93e75b2d7f (branch feat/trigger-include-event; ls-remote matches). New commits only, no force-push.
  - 28beb9868e: builder reference no longer tells agents to set `include_event` (tool schema refuses it); `_refuse` parameter renamed `recorded_event`; tautological rollback test and task 1.4 removed; array test; spec: a template with a pill is always stored as text parts for `messages` (task 7.2, decision 10), array fixture, decision 9 table fixed, true reason for the Run now press-time read, "request body".
  - 77e6722047: CodeRabbit fixes (docs say which deliveries have `data.event`; `inputs_fields` tool text says an omitted mapping carries no event).
  - 93e75b2d7f: round 2 Low text fixes (one-pill and array spec scenarios, last `include_event` hint removed, "older deliveries").
- Records: https://github.com/Agenta-AI/agenta/pull/7911#issuecomment-6504955303 (slop, simplify), #issuecomment-6504955837 (correctness, security), #issuecomment-6504956231 (naming).
- CodeRabbit: 3 threads, all fixed, replied and resolved.
- Web impact (impl-web-event-picker told): compileMessageTemplate must store even one pill alone as a text part; shared fixtures gain an array case.
- Run files: review/7911/ (context.md, r1/r2 reports and findings, records).
- Not run: `openspec validate --strict` (no CLI on the box).

- The evtinc web image was rebuilt from the API worktree (private tag) because the uiplay retag had a different web lockfile.
- Screenshot not yet attached to the PR (claude-in-chrome not connected).

# Approved mockup (Mahmoud, 2026-10-29)

Automation detail card, event automation ("When a pull request is opened in GitHub").

1. Header: integration icon, event name in plain words, repo and agent name.
2. "Instruction" label, then the instruction box. Pills inline in the text, each with a field icon,
   the label, and an x to remove. Helper text under the box:
   "Sent to the agent each time this event happens. Fields fill in with the real values."
3. Row: "Add details from the pull request" (left) and "Click to add" (right, muted).
   Grid of field cards (auto-fit, min 170px). Each card: label (bold) plus the Composio
   description (muted, small). A used field shows a check and reads dimmed.
4. Checkbox, on by default: "Also attach the full event, so the agent can use any detail"
5. Divider, then "What the agent gets" with an eye icon and the muted note
   "from the last pull request event". A grey box shows the resolved message; when the
   checkbox is on, it adds the event block at the end.
6. Discard and Save buttons.

Labels: humanized field names (createdBy -> "Created by"). No hand-written label map.
The word after "Add details from the" is the event's noun; if no clean noun exists, use
"Add details from the event".

# Context for the review of PR #7911 (feat/trigger-include-event)

PR: fix(api): include the event in the agent's message for event automations.
Base: merge base with release/v0.127.1 = d2651bc1d96924d80e842c636feac54f5ce18a3d.
A frontend PR (feat/automation-event-field-picker) stacks on this branch. It is NOT in this diff.

The PR contains the API part and the full spec of the change at
`openspec/changes/attach-event-to-automation-runs/` (proposal, design, specs, tasks, and the
design review record `review-loop.md`). Review the spec files too. The design review stopped at its
3-round cap. Its round 3 fixes were never reviewed. Check them (listed at the end of this file).
Most of the spec describes the frontend PR; judge those parts as a design, against today's code.

Research notes: the PR author wrote them outside the repo. Do not ask for them.

## Settled product decisions (Mahmoud approved them; do not argue with these)

1. The event is included by default: `TriggerSubscriptionData.include_event: bool = True`, stored
   in the JSON `data` column. A row without the key reads as true. No migration.
2. The exact event text is `"\n\nEvent data (<event_type>):\n```json\n<json>\n```"`, appended to
   the last user message. The frontend computes the same text. Do not propose a format change.
3. No size cap on the event text (the cap was cut in the design review for lack of evidence).
4. Field cards from the Composio payload schema; a pill is stored as `$.event.attributes.<key>`.
5. A "What the agent gets" preview filled from the newest delivery, which is why each subscription
   delivery stores `data.event`.
6. Text coercion of pill values that are not strings (number, object, absent) for subscriptions only.
   Reason: a number field fails the run today.
7. The builder agent reference text fix in `agenta_builtins.py` and `op_catalog.py` stays in this PR.

## Repo rules reviewers apply

- Pre-PMF: do the least work and keep today's behavior unless a change is needed now or is a
  one-way door.
- No backward-compatibility shims or safety nets.
- No runtime flag injection.
- No invented user copy.

## Round 3 design fixes that no reviewer has checked yet

- `remapMessageTemplate` moves a template with pills when the input shape resolves late, for event
  automations (design decision 10, spec automation-event-fields, tasks 7.3, 7.8, 9.1).
- `compileMessageTemplate` (no caller today) changes in place to keep other keys; no second writer
  (design decision 10, tasks 7.2, 8.2).
- Pure `latestDeliveryEvent(deliveries)` in core, used by the preview and Run now; Run now awaits
  `queryTriggerDeliveries` itself (design decision 8, proposal, tasks 7.6, 9.1, 10.1).
- `parseMessageTemplate` returns `string | null` (design decision 10, task 7.2).
- Decision 9 folder text.
- Open question kept: the name `renderMessagePreview` for text that Run now also sends. Kept,
  because the preview and Run now send the same text by design.

## After round 1 (head 28beb9868e)
- Fixed: builder reference no longer tells agents to set `include_event` (the tool schema has no such key), in 28beb9868e.
- Fixed: spec says a template with a pill is always stored as text parts for `messages`, so an array field becomes JSON text (task 7.2, decision 10); array fixture added (decision 8, tasks 2.3, 7.8) and a backend test, in 28beb9868e.
- Fixed: `_refuse` parameter renamed `recorded_event`, in 28beb9868e.
- Fixed: tautological rollback test and task 1.4 removed; decision 9 table repaired; "request body" for the create request; design decision 8 now gives the true reason for the press-time read.
- Rejected: Run now reading `useAutomationRuns` instead of its own query. Reason: settled in design round 2; the press-time read uses the newest event when the user presses; the web PR already implements it.
- Rejected: one shared sort for `latestDeliveryEvent` and `sortRuns`. Reason: `@agenta/entities` cannot import `@agenta/automation-ui`; both sort by `created_at`; the preview and Run now share `latestDeliveryEvent`.
- Rejected: merging `remapMessageTemplate` into `remapMessageShape`. Reason: they read and write different stored forms.
- Rejected: a helper for the dispatcher's resolve-wrap-compose steps. Reason: schedules skip compose; a helper needs a kind flag.
- Rejected: renaming parse/compile helpers to get/set. Reason: they are existing exports; out of scope.
- Rejected: renaming `compose_event_inputs`. Reason: the docstring states the coercion and both subscription paths always call it.

Round 2: check that the fixes above are correct and complete, and look for new problems the fixes added. Do not raise a rejected item again unless you show the reason is wrong.

## CodeRabbit, handled before round 2 (head 77e6722047)
- Fixed: the reference doc says which deliveries record `data.event`; the `inputs_fields` tool description says the event goes into the last user message in `messages` and that an omitted mapping carries no event. In 77e6722047.
- Declined: adding `include_event` to the create_subscription tool schema. Reason: the spec non-goal keeps the tool closed; builder agents get the default.

# PR #7911, interfaces lens (design-interfaces), round 1

Checkout: /data/mahmoud/review-7911.wt/r1-claude-interfaces, head 67e486bf8e, base d2651bc1d9.
Read: `api/oss/src/core/triggers/dtos.py` (full `TriggerSubscriptionData`, `TriggerScheduleData`,
`TriggerDeliveryData`, `TRIGGER_CONTEXT_FIELDS`), `api/oss/src/core/triggers/utils.py`,
`api/oss/src/tasks/asyncio/triggers/dispatcher.py`, `api/oss/src/apis/fastapi/triggers/models.py`,
`openspec/changes/attach-event-to-automation-runs/design.md`, and the builder agent surfaces that
describe the field (`sdks/python/agenta/sdk/agents/platform/op_catalog.py`,
`sdks/python/agenta/sdk/agents/adapters/agenta_builtins.py`).

## Field 1: `TriggerSubscriptionData.include_event: bool = True`

1. What is it? A switch. When it is true, the dispatcher appends the event text (`event_type`
   header and the JSON of `attributes`) to the last user message of the resolved inputs, or
   adds a user message, per the shape rules of design decision 3.
2. Who sets it? The user, through the subscription create and edit calls. The builder agent
   cannot set it (see finding F1). The platform supplies the default.
3. When does it change? Per subscription, when the user edits it. It is read once per dispatch.
4. Role: config of the mapping. It changes how `inputs_fields` resolves into the request inputs.
   It is not state, policy, credentials or routing.
5. Standard name: `include_` is the repo's verb for "add this to the result" (`include_archived`).
   Settled (context decision 1, design decision 1).
6. Will it grow? The design names no second option, and decision 1 rejects `event: {include}`
   nesting for that reason. A flat bool is right until a second option exists.
7. Can another engineer predict where it lives? Yes. It sits in the `MAPPING` block of `data`,
   right after `inputs_fields`, which it changes. It is not in `flags`, which holds run state
   (`is_active`, `is_valid`, `is_test`). `TriggerScheduleData` has no such field, which matches
   the non-goal "schedules". The parent describes the same kind of thing.

Settled, not raised: the default `True` (decision 1 and 2 of the context file), absent key reads

=== r1-codex-correctness.md
# Correctness review

Base: 93e75b2d7f434f731953df559b518cedeeb48ec3
Head: 161a3a3f4b173a9a44742ec06716e58e937edd33

## Findings

### 1. Literal text after a pill can disappear during delivery
- Severity: Medium
- Where: web/packages/agenta-entities/src/gatewayTrigger/core/eventMessageTemplate.ts:104; web/packages/agenta-entity-ui/src/gatewayTrigger/drawers/subscription/EventMessageComposer.tsx:40
- What is wrong: Enter `Review `, insert a URL pill, remove its trailing space, and append `/files`. The compiler stores `/files` as a separate text part. The backend resolves every string starting with `/` or `$` as a selector. An absent `/files` selector becomes null and then empty text. The actual automation loses the suffix, while the preview and Run now retain it. The new editor makes this existing compiler limitation reachable.
- Smallest fix: Preserve literal parts that start with selector prefixes. Split the initial `/` or `$` into a separate literal part after a preceding literal character, so no literal leaf starts with a selector prefix.

### 2. Copying and pasting an instruction loses its pills
- Severity: Medium
- Where: web/packages/agenta-entity-ui/src/gatewayTrigger/drawers/subscription/PillEditor.tsx:129
- What is wrong: Select an instruction containing a pill, copy it, and paste it into the editor. Native clipboard text contains the pill’s displayed label, not its `data-token` selector. The paste handler reads only `text/plain`, so the pasted instruction contains static label text instead of an event field. Saving it stops that field from resolving on later runs.
- Smallest fix: Add copy and cut handlers that serialize selected pills as their template tokens. Parse those tokens back into pills on paste.

## Rationale

Actual event deliveries can lose instruction text even when Run now shows the expected result. Ordinary copy and paste can also replace dynamic fields with static text.

Both problems affect specific editing flows and have local fixes. The review used source and test inspection only. No checks were run.

Rating: Medium=== r1-codex-security.md
# Security review

Base: 93e75b2d7f434f731953df559b518cedeeb48ec3
Head: 161a3a3f4b173a9a44742ec06716e58e937edd33

## Findings

No findings.

## Rationale

The new event preview and Run now use the existing deliveries endpoint. That endpoint checks `VIEW_TRIGGERS` and filters database reads by the request’s project ID and subscription ID. The change adds no permission bypass.

The editor renders field labels and event values as text. It creates text nodes for pills and accepts pasted content as plain text. The changed code does not execute event values or add a path that exposes credentials.

This was a static, read-only review. No tests or live services were run.

Rating: Low=== r1-codex-simplify.md
# Simplify review

Base: 93e75b2d7f434f731953df559b518cedeeb48ec3
Head: 161a3a3f4b173a9a44742ec06716e58e937edd33

## Findings

### 1. Derive pill labels directly from selectors

- Severity: Low
- Where: web/packages/agenta-entities/src/gatewayTrigger/core/eventFields.ts:44; web/packages/agenta-automation-ui/src/AutomationInstructionField.tsx:193
- What is wrong: Suggestion (non-blocking). The label map adds an unnecessary path through the composer and preview. Every card label comes from `fieldLabel(path)`. The fallback in `selectorLabel` produces the same label from the selector. Run now already uses this fallback with an empty map. No caller supplies a separate label policy.
- Smallest fix: Remove `eventFieldLabels` and the `labels` parameters and props. Use the selector-derived label for pills and previews. Keep labels on the field cards. This preserves the approved humanized labels and removes the catalog dependency from pill labeling.

## What to keep

Keep the shared preview renderer, the fresh delivery query on Run now, and the existing draft state for `include_event`. Keep the separate schedule and event composers: their content rules differ, so merging them would add conditions.

This was a static review. No files were changed, and no checks were run.

Rating: Low=== r1-codex-slop.md
# Slop review

Base: 93e75b2d7f434f731953df559b518cedeeb48ec3
Head: 161a3a3f4b173a9a44742ec06716e58e937edd33

## Findings

### 1. Run now cannot send an event-only instruction
- Severity: Medium
- Where: web/mobile/src/features/automations/runNowText.ts:24; web/mobile/src/features/automations/AutomationTestRunButton.tsx:55
- What is wrong: Clear the instruction, leave “Also attach the full event” checked, and save an automation with a recorded event. The preview shows the event text. Run now remains disabled because its guard checks the empty stored instruction. The new helper also returns early for `{}`, so fixing the guard alone would still send no event. This breaks the approved preview/Run now contract.
- Smallest fix: Let an empty event mapping reach the shared renderer. Check whether the resolved message is empty before starting the session. Apply this to both Run now entry points.

### 2. Copy and paste lose event-field pills
- Severity: Medium
- Where: web/packages/agenta-entity-ui/src/gatewayTrigger/drawers/subscription/PillEditor.tsx:129
- What is wrong: Copy or cut an instruction containing a pill, then paste it into the editor. There is no copy handler to preserve the selector stored in `data-token`. Paste reads only `text/plain`, so the pill becomes ordinary display text or disappears from the copied text. Saving then loses the field substitution. The helper tests do not exercise this editor path.
- Smallest fix: Serialize selected pills as template tokens during copy and cut. Reconstruct those tokens as pills during paste. Add coverage for copying and moving an instruction containing a pill.

## Rationale

The new renderer supports event-only messages, but the Run now integration excludes them. A valid saved configuration therefore shows a message that the user cannot test.

The custom editor stores field meaning in DOM attributes but does not preserve it through clipboard operations. Ordinary editing can silently change the saved instruction. Both problems need focused fixes; the core approach can remain.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.
